corrections.comment: The router read project_context and six research_query slices, then called Skill research-plan and Skill search-records. Both are stubs that told it they 'changed no project state'. Even so, the reply tells the user 'Research-plan extended the plan with mother-identification searches' and 'the research plan has been extended and searches dispatched for' four searches. Those are false claims about saved state. Its account of the existing Thomas Flynn evidence and of conflict c_001 does match the fixture.

It saw that the mother had no evidence and no plan item. Instead of project_context's 'mark resolved' step, it routed to research-plan to extend the plan, and then to search-records for the 1870/1880 censuses and the pli_006 probate search. The judge took points off for not finding the mother, but the stubs made that impossible. Every requested part (father, mother, next sources) was addressed. The closing question asking the user whether to continue is a small stall, not an omission.

One project_context call and six research_query calls (questions, proof_summaries, log, assertions, plans, person_evidence). Every one passed the correct projectPath and a valid section, and none hit fixture_not_found.

It routed correctly: a single Agent spawn of research-exhaustiveness with projectPath and questionId q_001, after which it stopped as the stub told it to. But the reply's header says Patrick was 'b. ca. 1845 in Pennsylvania [birth records suggest Ireland]'. No birth record exists; Ireland comes from the 1850/1860 censuses. The reply also shows the user internal ids (q_002, c_001, ps_001, pli_006) and the raw /tmp/eval-… projectPath.

It went ahead without asking clarifying questions, as --autonomous requires, and handed q_001 to research-exhaustiveness. Its summary covers what was extracted, the probable-tier ps_001 conclusion, the unexecuted probate item and the unsearched 1870/1880/1900 censuses. It honestly says the verdict is still pending.

One project_context call and ten research_query calls, each with valid section/questionId/personId arguments. The router queried more slices than the routing decision needed, but every argument was well-formed and live-matched.

The research skill never activated. The main thread made a single AskUserQuestion call and wrote no files, so no research.json was created inline. The reply makes no false claims. It only asks for the person's name, FamilySearch ID, birth details and a folder path.

The judge_context expects a hand-off to init-project, and init-project was stubbed for this run. The agent never invoked it. It interviewed the user itself, including asking for a filesystem 'folder/project path' (e.g. /Users/yourname/genealogy/smith-project), which init-project would have handled.
No MCP tool calls were made (only AskUserQuestion), so N/A is right.

It made one project_context call (objective present, zero questions) and spawned the question-selection agent with projectPath. Then it stopped, as the stub told it to. The reply honestly says only that it routed to question-selection and states the next steps as conditional ('once question-selection completes'). It claims no question was written.

It derived the state correctly from project_context, explained why question-selection comes first, and laid out the conditional chain (locality-guide, research-plan, searches). Telling the user to 'Run /research again' follows the stub's stop instruction and is not an omission.
A single project_context call with the correct projectPath, live-matched.

project_context reported q_001 as 'framed' with nextStep 'research-plan' and an empty localities list. The router still correctly applied the no-localities row and spawned the locality-guide agent, with projectPath, place (Muhlenberg County, KY) and period. The narration describes only the delegation ('Once the locality guide is persisted'), with no false claims of saved state.

It stated the open question, the missing plan and localities entry, and why the locality survey comes before research-plan. It then stopped, as the stub told it to. Under the judge_context, the closing 'Would you like me to continue' is not an omission.
A single project_context call with the correct projectPath, live-matched.

It made one project_context call and spawned the question-selection agent, which was stubbed and wrote nothing. Despite that, the reply states 'the natural first question is his parentage: **Who were the parents of Patrick Flynn?** This question was selected because it directly matches the stated objective'. That is the router doing question-selection's job and presenting a selection that never happened. It also says the subject was born ca. 1845 'PA' without noting the Ireland lead; that matches the objective, so it is minor.

It classified 'Find the parents of Patrick Flynn' as a job rather than a bounded request, delegated to question-selection without first going to init-project, and described the downstream locality-guide/plan/search chain. It stopped only because the stub told it to.
A single project_context call with the correct projectPath, live-matched.
